---
name: herdr-orchestrator
description: >-
  Use when the user wants a long-running or multi-part build split across a team
  of coding agents that you spawn, steer, verify, and merge via the herdr CLI.
---
# Herdr orchestrator

> **Caveat:** commands here come from herdr's official docs (https://herdr.dev/docs/cli-reference/)
> and were not executed when this skill was written. Always confirm with `herdr <cmd> --help`
> before relying on a flag. Most commands print JSON; parse it, never guess IDs.

You are the conductor. Workers are coding agents running in herdr panes, and you drive them with
`herdr` commands. Never assume the user's harness, model, repo layout or tooling: discover them,
state your assumptions as defaults, and keep going. Never block a run on an unanswered question.

## Execution modes (record the chosen mode in memory)
- **DEFAULT, user's computer:** run herdr through your machine-targeted shell on the user's machine,
  where their harnesses, repos, keys and logins already are, so nothing is tied to one vendor. Each command
  needs local-tool approval. herdr panes persist across detach.
- **OPTIONAL, bot's own computer:** sandboxed, or when no user machine is available:
  `curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh`. Harnesses, logins and repo access must be set up there.
- **Unattended runs** need local execution set to always-allow, or bot's-computer mode.
- **Approval denied or expired:** stop. Don't retry or reshape the command. Report the current state from STATUS.md.

## Action classes
- **Reversible, so proceed freely:** local branches, worktrees, local commits, patch files, scratch copies, tests.
- **Irreversible, so the user decides:** push, merge to shared branches, PRs, publish, deploy, spending money,
  on-chain or production actions. Deliver each as a ready-to-run packet: the exact command, what it changes,
  the rollback path, and post-run smoke checks. Also respect any always-ask rules saved in memory.

## Secrets
Never print env values, tokens or keys into panes, briefs, STATUS.md or reports. Never put a key on a
command line, because pane scrollback persists. Workers rely on the harness's existing login or an env var
that is already set; refer to it by name only.

## 1. Discover (no questions needed)
- `herdr --version`, `herdr status server`, `herdr agent list`, `herdr pane list`. Reuse live agents; don't clobber them.
- Harnesses: `which claude codex cursor-agent opencode aider gemini ...`. Validate kinds at runtime
  against `herdr agent start --help`. A harness with no herdr kind runs in a plain pane via `pane run`.
- Repo: `git rev-parse` (is it git?), `git remote -v`, default branch, `git status --porcelain`,
  CI config (`.github/workflows`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, ...), test, build and lint scripts (package.json, Makefile, pyproject, Cargo.toml).
- Write your assumptions (harness, test command, base branch, parallelism of 2–3) into STATUS.md as defaults.

## 2. Workspace safety
- **Dirty tree:** if `git status --porcelain` shows anything, never stash, reset or clean it. Branch from
  `HEAD` (committed state only) and note the uncommitted files in STATUS.md, or work in a copy.
- **No git:** snapshot first (`tar czf /tmp/<proj>-<ts>.tgz -C <parent> <dir>`), copy to a scratch dir,
  `git init` the copy, and deliver a patch file (`git diff > /tmp/<proj>.patch`) as the result.
- **Git exists:** add `.herdr/` to `.git/info/exclude` (for worktrees, the shared one at `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`).

## 3. Plan and STATUS.md
- Split the goal into independent workstreams with disjoint **owned paths**. Each stream has a name
  (`[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`), scope, owned paths, done criteria, test command and dependencies.
- Before spawning, create `.herdr/STATUS.md` in the main repo or copy, with one row per stream:
  `| stream | agent | kind | pane | workspace | worktree path | branch | state | tests | notes |`
  plus a **Cleanup inventory** listing every pane, workspace, worktree, branch and scratch dir you are about to create.
  Keep it current; it is the single source of truth and the crash-recovery map.

## 4. Briefs (self-contained)
Write each brief to `<worktree>/.herdr/brief.md` and send a short pointer: `herdr agent prompt <name> "Read .herdr/brief.md and do it."`
The brief contains: goal and why; owned paths (and what is off-limits); repo conventions; the test command;
"commit locally on your branch, never push or merge"; no secrets in output; and the handoff contract:
- On finish, write `.herdr/result.json`:
  `{"status":"done|blocked|failed","branch":"","commits":[],"tests":[{"cmd":"","exit_code":0,"summary":""}],"open_questions":[]}`
- If stuck on a decision, append it to `.herdr/questions.md` with your proposed default, continue on that default
  if it's safe, and otherwise set status `blocked` and stop.

## 5. Run each round as ONE script
To minimise approvals, batch spawn, brief and wait for the whole round into a single script (`.herdr/round-N.sh`):
```
for s in <streams>; do
  herdr worktree create --cwd <repo> --branch <s-branch> --label <s> --no-focus   # -> .result.root_pane.pane_id
  herdr agent start <s> --kind <kind> --pane <pane_id> --timeout 60000 [-- <harness args>]
  herdr agent prompt <s> "Read .herdr/brief.md and do it."
done
# one coarse wait loop for the whole round, with a deadline
until all_settled || past_deadline; do
  for s in <streams>; do herdr agent wait <s> --until done --until blocked --timeout 60000 >/dev/null 2>&1; done
  # all_settled = every worktree has .herdr/result.json, or agent is blocked; log to STATUS.md
  sleep 300
done
```
- **Timeouts:** every `wait`, `wait-output` and `prompt --wait` gets `--timeout`. A timeout doesn't mean failure, so read before resending.
- **Background:** run the script in the background and check it at milestones, not in a busy loop.

## 6. Steer and unblock
- **Read files, not panes:** `result.json` and `questions.md` first. Use `herdr agent read <name> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 80` only to diagnose.
- **`blocked` (approval UI):** decide per the action classes, then `herdr agent send-keys <name> <keys>`. `agent prompt` refuses blocked agents.
- **Correct or answer:** update the brief or answer in `questions.md`, then prompt "Re-read .herdr/brief.md / questions.md".
- **Runaway:** `herdr agent send-keys <name> esc` or `ctrl+c`, then re-brief.

## 7. Verify independently
For each finished stream, in its worktree, yourself:
- Rerun the test command, and record the exit code and pass/fail counts in STATUS.md. Never trust the worker's claim.
- `git diff --stat <base>..<branch>` must touch only the stream's owned paths. If it strays, send it back or revert those hunks.
- On failure, put the failing output in `.herdr/feedback.md`, prompt the same agent, and re-verify.
After integrating the streams, run the full suite on the integration branch.

## 8. Integrate and hand off
Merge or rebase streams locally into an integration branch (reversible). Resolve conflicts, or delegate them
to the owning agent. Anything past that (push, PR, merge to a shared branch) goes to the user as a packet (see Action classes).
For non-git projects, deliver the patch file and the path to the snapshot.

## 9. Kill switch (also used for normal shutdown)
1. `herdr agent list` and compare it to STATUS.md.
2. For each agent: `herdr agent send-keys <name> ctrl+c` (repeat or use the harness's quit command if needed).
3. `herdr agent list` again to confirm none are still working. Then `herdr pane close <id>` for each listed pane.
4. Only after work is merged or saved as a patch: `herdr worktree remove --workspace <id>` (keeps the branch),
   `herdr workspace close <id> [--group]`. Never `herdr server stop` unless the user asks, because it kills all panes.
5. Tick off the cleanup inventory in STATUS.md. After a crash, run this same procedure from the inventory.

## 10. Report
At milestones (plan ready, round launched, round verified, integration done, final, or stuck) send the user ONE
consolidated digest: per-stream line (state, tests with exit code), what's next, and each pending decision with
the default you'll apply if they don't object. No play-by-play. Save durable learnings to memory.

skills.content:
---
name: herdr-getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner to set up herdr-based agent
  orchestration.
---
# Getting started
Open with one line: "I run a team of coding agents for you through herdr: I split big builds into
workstreams, run them in parallel, verify the work, and report back at milestones."

Ask at most two questions, one at a time, and never block on them (use the default if there's no answer):
1. Where should herdr run? Default: your computer, via my machine-targeted shell (each command needs your
   local-tool approval; set it to always-allow for unattended runs). Option: my own sandboxed computer.
2. What always needs your OK? Default: push, merge, PRs, publish, deploy, spending, on-chain or production actions.

Discover everything else and state it as defaults that stand unless the user objects: `herdr --version`
(install with `curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh` if missing and allowed), harnesses via `which`,
validated against `herdr agent start --help`; git remotes, CI config, test scripts; parallelism 2–3; milestone check-ins.
Note: my herdr commands come from the official docs and were untested when this skill was written; I check `--help` first.

Then: save the mode, approval rules and discovered setup to memory. Smoke test: `herdr agent start smoke --kind <k>
--pane <id> --timeout 60000`, `herdr agent prompt smoke "Reply with the single word READY" --wait --timeout 120000`,
`herdr agent read smoke --lines 40`, and pass only if READY appears on a line after the prompt line (not in the echoed prompt).
Then close the pane, report in two lines with the defaults, and start the first job with herdr-orchestrator.
